title: Strongly complete sets and a conjecture of Erdős
summary: A set $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is called $\textit{complete}$ if every sufficiently large integer can be written as a sum of distinct elements of $A$. It is $\textit{strongly complete}$ if it remains complete after one deletes finitely many elements from it. Building on recent work of Bergelson and Simmons and that of Griesmer, we establish a new strong-completeness criterion exploiting a three-component partition of a given set.
